Package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware

@NullMarked package io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware
The board's own hardware and program-wide introspection: ArduinoUno and ArduinoNano hand out the board's pins, I2C bus, USB mouse, LED matrix, clock, BoardModel (which board the program was compiled for) and BoardMemory (Juno's arena and the program's flash usage). Board I/O has one subpackage per interface: gpio holds the pin-level digital/analog operations, i2c the I2C register access, serial Serial, imu the device-independent inertial sensing contracts, motor the board-independent motor contracts, drive two-motor drive coordination, and net the Wi-Fi networking stack and time the Clock interface. The Java-facing hardware API that Juno's compiler recognizes as intrinsics.

Every operation here is declared as ordinary Java — a native method, or a plain static method built only from other supported operations — so a program using this API still compiles and reads like normal Java. At link time, Juno's linker/backend recognize the native methods (see IntrinsicRegistry) and emit their Arduino C++/assembly implementation directly, instead of requiring a JVM to interpret them. There is no runtime reflection, dependency injection, or driver discovery: the mapping from a Java call to generated hardware code is fixed and closed-world.

The API lives in subpackages, grouped by the hardware or concern they address:

  • hardware — the board's own peripherals, handed out by ArduinoUno: general-purpose I/O (hardware.gpio, Gpio, DigitalOutput), I2C (hardware.i2c), serial port I/O (hardware.serial), USB HID mouse control (hardware.hid), device-independent inertial sensing (hardware.imu), board-independent motor contracts (hardware.motor), two-motor drive coordination (hardware.drive), the UNO R4 WiFi's built-in LED matrix with its frame/canvas helpers and bitmap fonts (hardware.led), and program-wide introspection: arena and flash usage (BoardMemory) and the board the program was compiled for (BoardModel), the Wi-Fi/UDP/HTTP/JSON/email networking stack (hardware.net, hardware.net.http, hardware.net.email) with the SntpClock configuration for the internet-backed LocalDateTime.now() subset, and the monotonic uptime clock (hardware.time, Clock), for measuring elapsed time without blocking, and attached shields, sensors and devices (hardware.device): grove (the passive Grove Base Shield pin map and allocation-free Grove sensor drivers), lcd (character LCD shields), tft (the ELEGOO 2.8" TFT touch shield and its parallel bus), imu, servo, ir, sd and kasa.
  • remote — remotely controlled third-party ecosystems: lego (Powered Up, RCX and Power Functions).
  • util — general-purpose utilities: blocking millisecond/microsecond delays (Delay), seeded pseudorandom numbers (Random) and UUID byte conversion (UuidCodec), plus views, navigation and a frame-loop controller for multi-screen TFT programs (util.mvc).

Classes in this package and its subpackages are final, non-instantiable utility types (or, for a handle like DigitalOutput, a zero-cost wrapper around a primitive pin number) with no shared mutable state of their own: Juno has no heap for general object graphs, so the API is deliberately kept close to the primitive operations the generated firmware actually performs.

An entry-point class selects its compilation target with a @Board annotation and then calls into this API from main.

    The built-in LED matrix of the UNO R4 WiFi (12x8) and the UNO Q (13x8): LedMatrix, the raw begin/loadFrame/clear operations that ArduinoUno.getLedMatrix() hands out, and LedCanvas, a boolean[HEIGHT][MAX_WIDTH] pixel buffer with shape and text drawing helpers that render into it and send it to the board's matrix with show.
